dedupe_keys.name: usda school food authority survey on supply chain disruption and student participation school year 2024 25

description: This dataset holds responses to the fourth national survey of supply chain problems faced by School Food Authorities, the bodies that run school meals under the US National School Lunch Program. The survey was run by the USDA Food and Nutrition Administration in spring 2025 and the data were published on the USDA Ag Data Commons in August 2026. It was emailed to all 18,531 public, private and charter School Food Authorities operating the programme in school year 2024-25, and 69 percent responded. Questions cover supply chain challenges, their effects on meal operations and costs, and the strategies used to cope, alongside student participation. The study team cleaned the data, linked them to administrative data from the FNS-742 form and to the NCES Common Core of Data to classify urbanicity, and computed weights for nationally representative estimates. The file, about 1 MB, is free to download online and is in the US public domain. Caveats: answers are self-reported by staff, and earlier survey rounds must be combined for trends. Simulation uses: prevalence of supply disruptions and coping strategies among institutional food services for food supply resilience models. Related records: the Weekly Retail Food Sales series (data-weekly-retail-food-sales-p02909) and the Food Environment Atlas (data-food-environment-atlas-p02896) are other USDA food system data.
